_source: A Researcher's Guide to: Combustion Science (NASA, Oct 2015), ISS mini-book PDF
_note: Paraphrased summary of the guide's per-experiment table. Experiments the guide does not cover (CFI, BASS-II, Saffire, SAME-R, CFI-G) are omitted. 2015 expectations (e.g. ACME 'expected 2016') are the guide's, not PSI's.

PSI-69.objective: Heptane and methanol droplet flammability limits in O2/N2 mixtures with added inert suppressants
PSI-69.dates: ISS; operating at time of guide

PSI-68.objective: Follow-on to FLEX: broader fuels and surrogates, soot, slow convective flows, droplet interactions

PSI-26.objective: Burning and extinction of solid samples; whether materials burn as well or better in microgravity with adequate ventilation
PSI-26.hardware: MSG using the SPICE flow duct

PSI-102.objective: Particle-size distribution of smoke from spacecraft materials, to inform smoke detector design

PSI-47.objective: Background aerosol particulate levels on the ISS

PSI-107.objective: Transition from non-sooting to sooting flames, to support simple predictions of soot emissions

PSI-106.objective: Lifting and lifted flames, supporting fuel efficiency and lower pollutant emissions

PSI-20.objective: Materials flammability (ignition and extinction) and test relevance for low and partial gravity, using a gas-fed porous burner to simulate solid and liquid fuels

PSI-21.objective: Predictive accuracy for sooty pure-fuel and near-extinction dilute flames using lifted coflow flames

PSI-22.objective: Flame-ion production and electric-field (up to 10 kV) control of non-premixed flames

PSI-23.objective: Structure, dynamics and extinction of sooty and soot-free spherical flames

PSI-10.objective: Soot inception and control in oxygen-enriched non-premixed flames
